a series of 2',5',6'-trisubstituted 2,4- diamino-5,6,7,8-tetrahydropyrido[2, 3-d]pyr imidines have been designed as inhibitors of the DHFRs from P. cariniii, T. gondi, and rl.

the 2,4- diamino-6-(2'-chloro-5'-methylaminomethyl) pyrido[2, 3-d]pyr imidine 8, a new analogue of trimethoprim, was found to be a potent and selective inhibitor of the dihydrofolate reduc tase of Pneumocysts carini.

a series of 2',4'-diamino-6-[2-(aryl)-2-oxo-ethyl]-pyrido[2-3-d]pyrmiidines were synthesized as inhibitors of P. carinini, T. gondi and rlDHFR and were also evaluated as anti-opportunistic infection and anti-cancer agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a series of 2',5',6'-trisubstituted pyrido[2, 3-d]pyri midines as inhibitors of DHFR from pathogenic protozoan parasites.

the development of a series of pyrido[2,2-d]pyrimides with selectivity toward pathogen DHFRs as antiopportunisitic infection agents and with the development of pyrido[3,2-d] pyrimidine analogues with potential as antitumor agents.
the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel pyrimidopyrimidine derivatives with potential as inhibitors of opportunistic infections and as antitumor agents.

2,4,6-trisubstituted 2,4- diamino-pyrido[2, 3-d]pyridimidines are a promising class of compounds for the development of selective inhibitors of pathogenic DHFR and as potential antipathogen and antitumor drugs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
2,4,6-substituted pyrido[2, 3-d]pyridimines with a 2',5-dichlorophenyl substituent at N10 are promising leads for further optimization.
the 2,4- diamino-5-substituted pyrido[2, 3- d]pyrimidine series is a promising lead series for the discovery of selective inhibitors of pcDHFR and/or tgDHFR.
the 2,4,5-trisubstituted analogues are less potent than the 2,5-diamino-4-substituted analogues against the three enzymes and the selectivity for pathogenic enzymes is greater.
The main takeaway from our work is that
compounds 4-16 are selective against pcDHFR and/or tgDHFR and that the 2',5-dichloro analogue is a promising starting point for the development of novel antiopportunistic infections agents.
2,4- diaminopyrido[2.3-d]pyrindines with a 5-phenyl side chain are less potent than 5-methyl analogs against all three DHRFs but show selectivity for pathogenic DHFR from P. cariniii and T. gondi.
compounds 8 and 9 are potent inhibitors of pcDHFR and are promising leads for the development of anti-PCP drugs.
